import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Maximality of $k = 43$ with restricted digit counts in bases $3 \le b < k$

Numbers $k$ such that the base $b$ expansion of $k$ for each
$b = 3..k-1$ never contains more than two distinct digits.

The sequence Numbers $k$ such that the base $b$ expansion of $k$ for each
$b = 3..k-1$ never contains more than two distinct digits.

*References:*
- [A306424](https://oeis.org/A306424)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA306424


open List Finset Nat

/--
Numbers $k$ such that the base $b$ expansion of $k$ for each
$b = 3..k-1$ never contains more than two distinct digits.
-/
def Condition (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  -- The bases $b$ range over $3 \le b \le k-1$, expressed as $3 \le b$ and $b < k$.
  ∀ b : ℕ, 3 ≤ b ∧ b < k → ((Nat.digits b k).toFinset.card) ≤ 2

/--
The $n$-th number $k$ such that the base $b$ expansion of $k$ for each
$b = 3..k-1$ never contains more than two distinct digits.
-/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ := n.nth Condition


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by sorry

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by sorry

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 3 := by sorry

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 4 := by sorry

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 5 := by sorry


/--
Conjecture: The sequence is finite, with 43 being the last term.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/306424.wip.lean#L276"]
theorem forty_three_is_max : Condition 43 ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 43 < k → ¬Condition k := by
    sorry

end OeisA306424

reformulations.difference: The definition uses zero-indexed Nat.nth and permits Condition 0, whereas OEIS lists positive terms with offset 1. Nat.nth also supplies zero outside the finite enumeration.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Condition 0 holds vacuously and 0 precedes every positive qualifying number. Thus inserting 0 exactly compensates for Nat.nth's zero-based indexing: a n agrees with OEIS at every defined index 1 ≤ n ≤ 23. In scratch.lean, check_bfile proves all 23 listed values, and positive_index_iff proves equivalence with the one-based enumeration of positive qualifying numbers. No statement in the file uses the out-of-range zero values.

reformulations.difference: The source says the sequence is finite with last term 43; Lean asserts that 43 qualifies and every larger natural number fails, without a separate finiteness conjunct.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The Lean upper bound places all qualifying positive numbers in {1,…,43}, hence makes their set finite, and Condition 43 makes 43 its greatest element. Conversely, having greatest element 43 gives both conjuncts of the Lean statement. Allowing 0 in Condition does not affect this equivalence. The exact equivalence with finiteness and IsGreatest for the positive qualifying set is proved as maximality_iff_source_finiteness in scratch.lean.

review.notes: Checked both definitions, all five test lemmas, and the main theorem. The digit bounds, per-base quantification, and distinct-digit count match OEIS. Boundary checks and all 23 OEIS terms were kernel-checked without using the file's sorry-backed lemmas. The main OEIS page was blocked by Cloudflare, so its complete entry was read from the official OEIS data mirror. OEIS explicitly reports a proof on June 1, 2026, consistent with the research solved tag. The cited historical proof has the same statement and no explicit sorry or custom axioms. Its older helper tactics did not compile unchanged on the current toolchain; proof-recheck.lean reuses its large-number construction and replaces the finite-check helpers with direct verified computation. The resulting exact maximality theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
